best_architecture:
RECOMMENDED: A two-tier architecture. Tier 1 (default, ship this) = Docker Compose as the baseline orchestrator; Tier 2 (optional migration path) = k3d (k3s-in-Docker) for when autoscaling/HA is needed. Reasoning below.

WHY COMPOSE FIRST FOR LOCAL-CLAW: The Local-Claw stack (Unsloth/Gemma inference server + Qwen fallback, TypeScript MCP bridge, Python MCP client, skill workers, MongoDB, Chroma, Redis) is a single-node, single-GPU (RTX A6000 48GB) workload. Docker Compose is the correct baseline because: (1) GPU passthrough is trivial and stable via the `deploy.resources.reservations.devices` block (driver: nvidia, count: all/1, capabilities: [gpu]) plus nvidia-container-toolkit on the host with driver >= 525.60.11 -- no custom node image, no device-plugin chain, no RuntimeClass; (2) service discovery by container name on a shared Docker network is enough for the MCP bridge to reach inference/Mongo/Chroma/Redis; (3) model weights persist trivially via a named volume mounted at /root/.cache/huggingface (or the Unsloth/HF cache dir), avoiding re-download on restart; (4) lowest operational overhead and fastest iteration for an agent project. Use `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` plus healthchecks to order startup (inference server needs long model-load probe timeouts before MCP bridge connects).

KEY COMPOSE DESIGN DECISIONS: separate services per concern (inference-server, mcp-bridge, skill-worker[s], mongodb, chroma, redis); named volumes for model-cache (HF/Unsloth), mongo-data, chroma-data, redis-data; only the GPU-bound inference service gets the device reservation (MCP bridge, workers, DBs stay CPU-only to leave VRAM for the model); set NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all and NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility on the inference service; avoid the legacy `runtime: nvidia` key (fails on modern setups with 'unknown or invalid runtime name'); use Compose profiles to optionally add the Qwen2.5-Coder-32B fallback only when needed; scale skill workers manually with `docker compose up --scale skill-worker=N`.

WHEN/HOW TO MIGRATE TO KUBE (Tier 2): Move to k3d (NOT kind, NOT plain kubeadm) only when you need declarative HA, namespace isolation, Helm-packaged releases, or event-driven autoscaling of skill workers. k3d is the right K8s-in-Docker choice for GPU because: kind does NOT support GPU passthrough (nodes are plain kubeadm containers; GPU is effectively unsupported); bare-metal k3s gives the easiest GPU but is not 'in Docker'; k3d wraps k3s in Docker and CAN pass GPUs with `k3d cluster create --gpus all` PLUS a custom NVIDIA-enabled k3s node image (the stock image is Alpine-based and the NVIDIA container runtime is not supported on Alpine -- you must rebuild on an Ubuntu base). CRITICAL GPU GOTCHA: k3s auto-detects the nvidia containerd runtime but leaves runc as the default, so pods start without driver libs and the device plugin fails with 'Failed to initialize NVML: ERROR_LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND' and the node advertises zero GPUs even though nvidia-smi works on the node. Fix: pass `--k3s-arg "--default-runtime=nvidia@server:*"` (and @agent:*) so nvidia is the default runtime; then either rely on the device plugin baked into the custom image or install the NVIDIA GPU Operator (recommended -- it manages drivers/toolkit/device-plugin/RuntimeClass and avoids version skew). Create a RuntimeClass named nvidia and set runtimeClassName: nvidia on GPU pods if not using --default-runtime.

KUBE STORAGE/SCALING DECISIONS: For model weights use a PVC backed by k3s's built-in local-path-provisioner (storageClassName: local-path, ReadWriteOnce), mounted at the HF cache path, so weights survive pod restarts -- combine with a StatefulSet (or nodeSelector/pod-affinity pinning) so the pod reschedules onto the same node and keeps the cache (a plain emptyDir is wiped on pod delete; local-path PVs are node-local). Package each service (inference, MCP bridge, Mongo, Chroma, Redis) as a Helm release -- use Bitnami charts for MongoDB/Redis and the official Chroma chart, and consider the vLLM production-stack Helm chart pattern as a reference for the inference tier (router + serving engine + PVC + autoscaling hooks). For skill-worker autoscaling prefer KEDA OVER plain HPA: HPA scales on CPU/memory which is meaningless for GPU/queue-bound work (a worker can be at 5% CPU while its queue is backed up), KEDA scales on the right signal (queue depth, e.g. Redis list length or vllm:num_requests_waiting) AND uniquely supports scale-to-zero to free the single A6000 when idle. Use HPA only as a complementary CPU-bound layer for the stateless MCP bridge. Apply namespace isolation (e.g. local-claw-inference, local-claw-data, local-claw-skills).

RUNPOD A6000 COMPATIBILITY (DECISIVE CONSTRAINT): A RunPod GPU pod is ITSELF a container, so running k3d means nested Docker-in-Docker WITH GPU -- this is the hard part. RunPod Clusters (multi-node) are explicitly NOT Kubernetes-compatible (they use RunPod's native orchestration + Slurm), so you cannot bring your own k8s across a RunPod cluster. On a single RunPod GPU pod, Compose-with-GPU works as long as /dev/nvidia* is exposed and the toolkit is present. Nested k3d/GPU requires the outer container to be privileged and to have the NVIDIA devices mounted; nested NVIDIA-runtime containers are known to fail with 'mount "proc" to "/proc": Operation not permitted' unless the outer container is privileged (mirrors the LXD-must-be-privileged finding). NET RECOMMENDATION FOR LOCAL-CLAW: ship Docker Compose as the production target on RunPod (reliable single-node GPU); treat k3d as a LOCAL dev/staging convenience and a future multi-node migration target, validating privileged-DinD GPU passthrough before committing to k3d on RunPod. [uncertain: exact RunPod privileged-container / DinD GPU support depends on RunPod's current Secure-Cloud vs Community-Cloud host policy and may require Community Cloud or a dedicated host]
reference_papers: KIS-S: A GPU-Aware Kubernetes Inference Simulator with RL-Based Auto-Scaling (Yang et al. 2025) - arxiv:2507.07932 - Triton-on-Kubernetes single-node GPU cluster (NVIDIA container runtime + GPU Operator), CPU/GPU partitioning and RL-based autoscaling; directly relevant to skill-worker autoscaling decisions

Resource Aware GPU Scheduling in Kubernetes Infrastructure (Ferikoglou et al. 2021) - OASIcs PARMA-DITAM 2021, DOI:10.4230/OASIcs.PARMA-DITAM.2021.4 - GPU-memory-aware colocation scheduler for inference; reports 105.9% higher GPU utilization and 44.4% lower energy vs treating GPUs as generic resources; motivates why default schedulers underuse a single A6000

Evaluating Kubernetes Performance for GenAI Inference: From Automatic Speech Recognition to LLM Summarization (2026) - arxiv:2602.04900 - applies K8s container-native design to heterogeneous GPU environments; covers Kueue batch scheduling, Dynamic Accelerator Slicer (DAS) for GPU slicing, and Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE)

Adaptive Orchestration for Large-Scale Inference on Heterogeneous Accelerator Systems: Balancing Cost, Performance, and Resilience (2025) - arxiv:2503.20074 - K8s HPA-driven orchestration with generic-request/label scheduling for GPU inference; relevant to Compose->kube migration and autoscaling design

GPU-enabled Function-as-a-Service for Machine Learning Inference (2023) - arxiv:2303.05601 - serverless/scale-to-zero GPU inference; supports the KEDA scale-to-zero argument for idle skill workers on a single GPU

ElasticRec: A Microservice-based Model Serving Architecture Enabling Elastic Resource Scaling (2024) - arxiv:2406.06955 - microservice model-serving with K8s HPA for QPS-target elastic scaling; analogous to per-service Helm + autoscaling layout
reference_repos: k3d-io/k3d - k3s wrapped in Docker; the recommended K8s-in-Docker tool for local GPU dev; see its official CUDA guide for custom node image + --gpus all - https://github.com/k3d-io/k3d (CUDA usage: https://k3d.io/v5.7.4/usage/advanced/cuda/)

88plug/k3d-gpu (a.k.a. cryptoandcoffee/k3d-gpu) - GPU-ready k3d clusters with CUDA + K3s on an Ubuntu base, NVIDIA device plugin baked into k3s auto-deploy, pre-configured --default-runtime=nvidia for zero-config GPU pods - https://github.com/88plug/k3d-gpu
NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin - DaemonSet that advertises nvidia.com/gpu capacity to the scheduler; required for any k3d/k3s GPU scheduling - https://github.com/NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin

NVIDIA/gpu-operator - automates driver, container-toolkit, device-plugin, RuntimeClass and DCGM install; recommended over manual device-plugin for k3d to avoid version skew - https://github.com/NVIDIA/gpu-operator

vllm-project/production-stack - K8s-native reference deployment of vLLM via a single Helm chart (serving engine + router + cache + PVCs + autoscaling hooks + Grafana); template for the inference tier - https://github.com/vllm-project/production-stack
bitnami/charts - production Helm charts for MongoDB and Redis (StatefulSets, PVCs, HA) usable directly for the Local-Claw data tier - https://github.com/bitnami/charts
amikos-tech/chromadb-chart (and chroma-core/chroma deploy manifests) - Helm chart / deployment manifests for Chroma vector DB on Kubernetes - https://github.com/amikos-tech/chromadb-chart
kedacore/keda - Kubernetes Event-Driven Autoscaling; queue-depth (Redis/Prometheus) scalers and scale-to-zero for skill workers - https://github.com/kedacore/keda
rancher/local-path-provisioner - default k3s dynamic local PVC provisioner used to cache model weights on-node across pod restarts - https://github.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner
open-webui/open-webui - reference docker-compose.gpu.yaml showing the parameterized nvidia device-reservation pattern for a local LLM Compose stack - https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui
quickpod/DockerInDocker - Docker-in-Docker with GPU passthrough patterns relevant to running nested k3d on a RunPod GPU pod - https://github.com/quickpod/DockerInDocker
key_libraries: Docker Engine + Docker Compose v2 (Go/CLI, Compose spec >= 3.4 for deploy.resources.reservations.devices) - baseline single-node orchestrator and the production target for Local-Claw on RunPod

nvidia-container-toolkit (C/Go, install on host; driver >= 525.60.11) - provides libnvidia-container so containers (and the k3s node container) get GPU access; required for both Compose --gpus and k3d
k3d (Go, v5.7.x) - creates k3s clusters inside Docker; supports --gpus all and --k3s-arg --default-runtime=nvidia for GPU nodes
k3s (Go, lightweight Kubernetes; bundles containerd + local-path-provisioner) - the cluster runtime k3d wraps
Helm (Go, v3.x) - package/deploy each service (inference, MCP bridge, Mongo, Redis, Chroma) as versioned releases across namespaces via values overrides
NVIDIA k8s-device-plugin (Go, e.g. v0.19.x) - DaemonSet exposing nvidia.com/gpu to the scheduler
NVIDIA GPU Operator (Go/Helm) - end-to-end GPU stack management (drivers, toolkit, device plugin, RuntimeClass, DCGM) on k3d/k3s
KEDA (Go, v2.x) - event-driven autoscaler with Redis-list and Prometheus scalers and scale-to-zero for skill workers
Kubernetes HPA (built-in, autoscaling/v2) - CPU/memory autoscaling, complementary layer for the stateless MCP bridge
local-path-provisioner (Go) - k3s default StorageClass (local-path) for model-weight PVCs that survive pod restarts
DCGM Exporter + Prometheus + Prometheus Adapter (Go) - GPU utilization/queue metrics pipeline feeding KEDA/HPA and observability
Bitnami Helm charts for MongoDB and Redis (Helm) - StatefulSet-based stateful service deployment with PVCs
vLLM Helm chart / vllm-project production-stack (Helm/Python) - reference inference-tier chart pattern (router + engine + PVC + autoscaling), adaptable to the Unsloth/Gemma server
